title: Bhai Taru Singh Explains Why the Guru’s Vow Cannot Be Undone

blocks.text: Continuing his reply, Taru Singh says one sheath cannot hold two swords and that two sovereign claims cannot share one throne. The image compresses the page's argument: the Khalsa's path and imperial domination cannot both be preserved intact, so sacrifice becomes the price of truth.

When the gathered Sikhs ask why the Gurus accepted such suffering, Taru Singh says the Guru's utterance cannot be erased because it was written in the divine court. What has been spoken and sealed in that higher register must be fulfilled even when fulfillment demands bodily loss.

He therefore insists that a Sikh cannot seek to save his own life after the Gurus have spent theirs for the community, while also pointing the sangat back toward the older history of Guru Nanak and Babur. The page becomes a threshold from Taru Singh's martyrdom into the larger retrospective explanation that follows.
